title: MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China
content:
Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

title: Nvidia Investors With $2.1 Billion at Stake Ask Board to Keep Jensen Huang’s Return on the Table
content:
Two investors whose funds held about $2.1 billion of Nvidia stock in June have asked its board not to rush into naming a new chief executive, and to keep Jensen Huang’s possible return open. Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, made their joint letter public on Friday.

In it, they urge the board to “pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang”. Nvidia has not responded publicly to the letter.

The request came a day after Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, while an investigation into his conduct was under way. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is now interim chief executive, and former Synopsys chief executive Harvey Jones became the board’s first chair, according to Nvidia’s announcement and its filing with US regulators . The letter also differs sharply from the viral “employee letter” that spread the same day, which copied OpenAI’s 2023 staff letter almost word for word. This one was published by the two investors who signed it.

The letter runs to four short paragraphs, and most of it argues against speed. “There are more questions about recent events than answers,” the two investors write. They say the board “should avoid a rush to replace Jensen that undermines and thwarts the best interests of shareholders”. In their view, the company “will be capably led in the interim by Colette Kress and team”, which means the board has time to get the decision right.

Gerstner and Baker also accept that the decision belongs to the board. “If after all the facts are known the Board decides that it is not in shareholders’ best interest to have Jensen Huang back as CEO, that is the Board’s prerogative,” the letter says. They add that Huang, as founder and long-time leader, “has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known”. The letter does not dispute the reports about Huang’s conduct, and it does not ask for him to be reinstated now.

Some viral summaries said the investors wanted “a more thorough investigation” before any decision. The letter does not use that phrase, and it does not mention the review led by former federal prosecutor Joon Kim and Wachtell Lipton , which the board’s independent directors commissioned before Huang left. It asks only that no successor be chosen before “all the facts are known”, and it sets no timetable. The board has not said when the review is expected to finish.

title: AMD Cuts Radeon GPU Supply in China by Up to 50%, and the Shortage Could Last Until January 2027
content:
AMD has cut supplies of Radeon gaming GPUs to its graphics card partners in China by 20% to 50% since October, according to Board Channels, a Chinese industry source that tracks the graphics card channel. The shortage could last until January 2027, the report adds. The cuts apply across the Radeon RX range rather than to a single model, and monthly allocations to board partners are still falling, MyDrivers reported on 12 November. AMD has not commented on the report, and it has not announced any change to its supply plans.

The report describes AMD’s shortage as no less severe than Nvidia’s. Nvidia’s board partners in China have also been working with limited GPU supply, and Nvidia has reportedly cancelled a 24GB RTX 5080 for the Chinese market because of memory costs. Nvidia’s RTX 50 cards use the newer GDDR7, and the 3GB modules that card needed cost about three times as much as the 2GB modules on the existing 16GB model. Taken together, buyers in one of the biggest markets for DIY PC parts face tight supply from both GPU vendors heading into the end of the year.

Board Channels points to two causes: rising costs for memory and GPU cores, and AI computing demand taking production capacity away from gaming parts. Every card in the current Radeon RX 9000 line-up uses GDDR6. The RX 9070 XT and RX 9070 carry 16GB on a 256-bit bus and the RX 9070 GRE has 12GB on a 192-bit bus, while the RX 9060 XT uses 8GB or 16GB on 128 bits. DRAM makers have shifted wafer capacity towards high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators, which tightens supply and raises prices for older graphics memory such as GDDR6. GPU vendors commonly sell their chips to board partners together with the memory, so those costs land on AMD’s allocations directly.

The pressure was already visible in AMD’s results. The company reported gaming revenue of $773 million for the third quarter, down 40% from a year earlier, which it put down to lower semi-custom and graphics revenue. Data centre revenue rose 97% to $8.5 billion in the same quarter. In May, AMD had already warned that higher memory and component costs would cut its second-half gaming revenue by more than 20% compared with the first half.

The supply cuts follow a run of price increases in China. AMD told partners in August that Radeon prices would rise by 10% or more, and new list prices took effect on 1 October, according to SMZDM . The RX 9070 rose by 700 yuan to 6,299 yuan, the RX 9070 GRE by 400 yuan to 4,999 yuan, and the RX 9060 XT 16GB by 600 yuan to 4,899 yuan. The RX 9060 XT 8GB went up by 300 yuan to 3,390 yuan, while the RX 9070 XT stayed at 6,999 yuan.

For board partners, the cut leaves fewer chips to build cards with. Brands that sell Radeon cards in China, from Sapphire, PowerColor and XFX to local makers such as Yeston, cannot ship products without GPU allocations, and MyDrivers said dealers have little stock to sell. Partners that also sell Nvidia cards have no easy fallback, since GeForce supply is tight as well.

title: Zupee Raised $100+ Million as a Gaming Company, When the Money Games Ended, It Called Itself AI
content:
Zupee told the market on 16 October that it was leaving gaming to build “AI-led” businesses for India. A month later, it has laid off its entire remaining workforce and looks close to shutting down, Inc42 reported , with severance covering staff until January 2027. Along the way, it closed its microdrama app Zupee Studio and its astrology platform NeoAstro. Investors had put more than $121 million into the company, roughly ₹1,000 crore at today’s exchange rate, on the promise that it was one of India’s leading gaming platforms.

The collapse was triggered by a law, not by a scandal, and nothing reported suggests Zupee broke any rules. Yet its rise and fall show how easily a fashionable label can stand in for a business. Zupee called itself a gaming company from 2018 until October, and when the money ran out it reached for the next label investors like. The question is what, beneath both labels, anyone was actually backing.

Zupee was founded in 2018 by Dilsher Singh Malhi and Siddhant Saurabh, two IIT Kanpur graduates. Malhi studied chemical engineering and worked as a research associate at EPFL in Switzerland, according to his IIT Kanpur profile , while Saurabh was a software engineer at the trading firm Graviton Research Capital. Neither had worked in games before Zupee, according to those profiles. The company started as a quiz app, then found its market in Ludo, Snakes and Ladders and Carrom, played for cash entry fees and cash prizes.

That model made serious money while it lasted. Zupee reported revenue of more than ₹1,100 crore and its first full-year profit, ₹146 crore, in the 2024 financial year, according to Entrackr . It closed a $102 million round in January 2022, with reports putting its valuation above $500 million, and signed a content partnership with Reliance Jio. Those numbers, however, came from players paying to compete for cash, not from players buying or playing games for their own sake.

The difference became obvious once paid contests ended. Zupee shut all of its paid games in August 2025 and kept free versions of Ludo Supreme, Ludo Turbo and Snakes and Ladders running. Without the entry fees, those games could not carry the company, and it cut about 170 jobs in September 2025 and about 200 more in January, YourStory reported . A business that loses its revenue overnight when cash prizes are removed was a contests business with games attached.

None of this should have surprised anyone writing cheques. Karnataka and Tamil Nadu both tried to outlaw real-money games before 2025. The 28% GST on the full value of deposits, in force since October 2023, showed how little goodwill the sector had left with policymakers. The industry’s defence rested on a label: these were games of skill, it argued, and so they were “gaming”, not gambling. Investors priced Zupee as a gaming platform, while its revenue depended on a legal distinction that the government could remove.

title: Man Arrested in Delhi Over Death of Kolkata Woman He Met Through PUBG
content:
Police have arrested Dharambir Kumar, a man from Uttar Pradesh, outside Anand Vihar railway station in New Delhi over the death of 26-year-old Anjali Shaw in Baranagar, north of Kolkata. Kumar was picked up late on 12 November in a joint operation by a special team from Baranagar police station and Delhi Police. According to police and her family, the two had met while playing PUBG. Kumar is being brought to West Bengal on transit remand for questioning, OJAS reported .

Shaw’s body was found with injury marks on the night of 10 November in a fifth-floor flat in the Lakepally area of Baranagar. The flat belongs to her elder sister and brother-in-law, who now live mostly in Srirampore, and it was empty at the time. Shaw had collected the key from a neighbour that afternoon, and police broke the door down that night after her sister could not reach her by phone, OJAS reported . Police have not disclosed the cause of death, and the case was first treated as a possible suicide before injuries and missing valuables pointed investigators towards a suspected murder. A cousin has alleged that she had injury marks on her neck and face.

Police suspect that a personal or financial dispute between the two may have led to her death, although they have not confirmed a motive. Police sources told OJAS they are also examining a disagreement over playing PUBG together. Shaw’s father said the pair were friends and that Kumar used to call her his sister, and he said Kumar had given his home address as somewhere near Lucknow. Kumar’s age has not been made public, and police have not said what charges he faces or whether he has a lawyer.

Kuntal Banerjee, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) of the Barrackpore Police Commissionerate, said the accused was being brought from Delhi and that his questioning would reveal more about the case. Investigators believe Kumar left with Shaw’s jewellery and mobile phone. Her family says the missing items include her watch, a ring, a bracelet and earrings. Investigators also say Kumar repeatedly switched the phone on and off after the incident, apparently to confuse attempts to track his location.

Police believe he used her phone to send WhatsApp messages to her father and to make a brief, silent call to her mother. Her family told OJAS that a reply from her number invited them to ask whatever they wanted. A second message then read, “I’m among you, but you won’t catch me.” The family handed screenshots of those messages to police, who traced Kumar through mobile tower data and other inputs.

Officers are reviewing CCTV footage from Shitala Mata Lane and Lakepally, partly to check whether anyone else was involved. Footage from the housing complex helped investigators identify the suspect earlier in the week, OJAS reported . Police have not named any other suspect, and they are also questioning family members, neighbours and other residents of the building. Local MLA Sajal Ghosh, who visited the family, said the culprit would be caught but that police needed time to complete the investigation.

title: PUBG MOBILE FLASH Is Out Worldwide: Under 1GB, Runs on 2GB RAM and Shares Your PUBG MOBILE Account
content:
PUBG MOBILE FLASH, the official lightweight version of PUBG MOBILE, is now available worldwide for free on Android and iOS. The app launched on 13 November with an initial download of 0.96GB on Android and under 2GB on iOS, and it runs on phones with as little as 2GB of RAM. It was co-developed by Tencent Games’ LightSpeed Studios and KRAFTON, and picked up 27 million pre-registrations before launch, according to the official launch announcement . Players who log in keep the same account, friends, matches and items they already have in PUBG MOBILE.

That last point is what separates FLASH from the old PUBG Mobile Lite. Lite, released in 2019 and since discontinued, used its own accounts and smaller matches, so players on budget phones were effectively cut off from everyone else. FLASH is a lighter client for the same game, with cross-play against the full app and updates synchronised with it. It was first shown at the PUBG Mobile World Cup in August as PUBG Mobile Light, before it was renamed FLASH in September.

The move targets the players PUBG MOBILE has found hardest to keep. Much of the audience it still wants to reach plays on budget Android phones with little free storage, in markets where Garena’s Free Fire built its lead by running on modest hardware. A sub-1GB client with a 2GB RAM floor brings PUBG MOBILE into that segment without splitting its player base, which was the main weakness of Lite.

The size saving comes from what FLASH leaves out of the first install. Only Erangel and Classic Battle Royale are pre-installed, while other maps, modes, events and higher-quality graphics packs are downloaded when players choose them, the press release says. A confirmation step stops those packs from downloading automatically, which matters on prepaid data plans. The lobby is simplified, icons are lightweight by default, and players who have not downloaded a cosmetic item see a temporary outfit in its place until they fetch the files.

Performance settings run at 25, 30, 40 or 60 frames per second, depending on the device. Compared with the FLASH beta, PUBG MOBILE says it is targeting a 10% higher average frame rate, 10% better frame-rate stability and 3% lower power use. It is also aiming for 12% less memory use, a 15% shorter startup screen and 20% faster loading before matches. The company describes those numbers as targets, not results guaranteed on every phone, so real gains will vary by chipset and storage speed.

Security is shared with the main game too. FLASH uses the same Ban Pan anti-cheat system as PUBG MOBILE, including real-time cheat detection, enforcement and its Investigator system. Since FLASH players share matches with players on the full game, PUBG MOBILE says they are covered by the same protections.

title: LoL Esports 2027: First Stand changes, all host cities
content:
Riot Games unveiled their plans for League of Legends (LoL) Esports in 2027. The first event of the year, First Stand: All In, promises to feature the most amount of teams in an international ever. It also announced the host cities for all international events, as well as a potential integration for the Demacia Cup into Worlds.

First Stand 2027 was initially announced for Southeast Asia . Riot has opted to move the event, now officially named First Stand: All In , to China.

MSI 2027 will take place in Valencia, Spain . This places it in the same city as the second VALORANT Masters of 2027, possibly reducing logistical and operational costs for the organizer.

Worlds 2027 will be split between two host countries and three cities: Nagoya, Japan , and Suwon and Seoul, South Korea .

Riot revealed the “All In” branding through a LoL Esports post. It said that with the change comes a major expansion and All In will be “a one-time event that will bring more teams, more players, and more of our global community together to kick off the competitive season.”

It also says that First Stand: All In 2027 will be the largest tournament Riot has ever produced. As part of this expansion, the event veers away from the initial plan of being hosted in Southeast Asia to China .

title: China approves Savvy Games Group’s $6B acquisition of Mobile Legends developer MOONTON Games
content:
China’s State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) has cleared Savvy Games Group’s parent entity Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company’s planned acquisition of MOONTON Games, the developer of Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB). This brings the reported $6 billion-plus deal with ByteDance one step closer to completion.

The approval, completed on Oct. 29 and published on Nov. 6, advances the acquisition that ByteDance agreed to in March 2026. Nearly eight months after the agreement was announced, the transaction has yet to close.

SAMR included the acquisition in its list of mergers approved without conditions between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1. The notice identifies Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company as the acquirer and Moonton Holdings Limited and Shanghai Moonton Technology Co., Ltd. as the target companies.

The notice does not mention Savvy Games Group by name. However, Saudi Electronic Games Holding Company is its parent entity, according to the Canadian trademark registration . Savvy is wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Savvy confirmed in March that it had signed an agreement to acquire Moonton from ByteDance for a reported price exceeding $6 billion. Neither company has disclosed the exact purchase price. ByteDance acquired MOONTON Games back in 2021 for approximately $4 billion before revealing its plans to restructure its gaming business in 2023.

The acquisition could have broader implications for esports. This is considering the number of major gaming and tournament organizations connected to Saudi Arabia’s PIP.

title: Solary peut vraiment débarquer en LEC ?
content:
Et si Solary faisait son entrée dans l’élite européenne de League of Legends ? La question se pose alors que Shifters, anciennement Team BDS, étudierait la possibilité de louer son slot en LEC pour la saison 2027. Une opportunité rare qui pourrait intéresser plusieurs structures, dont Solary, auteur d’une excellente année 2026 sur la scène française et européenne. Mais entre l’envie de franchir un cap et la réalité économique, le fossé semble encore important.

Interrogé à ce sujet lors d’un stream, César « Wakz » Hugues a préféré calmer les attentes. Le cofondateur de Solary reconnaît que l’idée est séduisante, mais difficilement réalisable avec les moyens actuels du club. « Dans notre situation, c’est très cher » , a-t-il expliqué, avant de préciser : « Actuellement, on se serre déjà la ceinture. » Une situation qui rendrait un tel investissement particulièrement risqué pour la structure tourangelle.

Selon les estimations de Wakz, faire fonctionner une équipe en LEC pendant une saison nécessiterait environ un million d’euros, avec une marge de 300 000 euros. En ajoutant le coût de location du slot de Shifters, l’investissement total pourrait grimper entre deux et cinq millions d’euros. Des montants difficilement envisageables pour Solary, qui avait déjà dû multiplier les initiatives pour faire face à 200 000 euros de dépenses imprévues liées à ses nouveaux locaux.

Une arrivée en LEC ne serait toutefois pas totalement exclue si des partenaires financiers décidaient de soutenir le projet. « Ce genre d’opportunités, c’est toujours possible si ce n’est pas nous qui mettons l’argent et qu’on peut avoir un sponsor pour » , a souligné Wakz. Le club pourrait également envisager certaines économies, notamment en utilisant les infrastructures de Shifters. Mais le constat reste clair : « En fonds propres, c’est impossible. » Avant de résumer la situation en quelques mots : « Il n’y a rien d’impossible, mais c’est peu probable. »

En attendant, Solary poursuit la construction de son effectif pour la prochaine saison de LFL. Après les départs attendus de Kryze et Zicssi vers SK Gaming, le club devrait notamment accueillir Boukada dans la jungle, ainsi que les Sud-Coréens Cypher et Thumb sur la botlane. Toffe a déjà été officialisé sur la midlane, tandis que Hairost fera son retour au poste de head coach.

title: Marvel Rivals ranks explained: All ranks, tiers, and progression details
content:
Ready to duke it out competitively in Marvel Rivals? Before jumping into the fray, you should understand how the different Marvel Rivals ranks and how the game’s progression system works. From Bronze all the way to One Above All, this guide covers every rank, how matchmaking works, and what you need to do to climb the ladder.

What are the ranks in Marvel Rivals? Marvel Rivals has nine ranks in total. These are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Grandmaster, Celestial, Eternity, and One Above All. Bronze is the lowest one possible and Marvel Rivals’ highest rank is One Above All.

The Bronze through Celestial ranks are divided into three tiers each. Meanwhile, the Eternity and One Above All ranks are the highest ones without additional tier divisions.

Marvel Rivals News Interview: Gabe Kunda as Blade in Marvel Rivals and a champion of the arts "It means the world. I don’t even think I can put into words how much this character means to me."

What ranks can play together in Marvel Rivals? Marvel Rivals uses competitive matchmaking restrictions to keep ranked games balanced. Players generally need to be within a certain rank range to queue together. Lower and mid-level ranks have more flexibility, allowing players close to each other on the ladder to form a party.

However, the restrictions become more noticeable at higher ranks to prevent large skill gaps between teammates. For example, a Bronze player cannot queue with a Grandmaster player because the difference in skill level would create unfair matches.

title: TSMC Confirms Employee Data Leak as Seller Offers 46,000 Records for 3 Bitcoin
content:
TSMC has confirmed that personal data belonging to some of its current and former employees was posted on an external website without authorisation, after a seller began offering what it claims are about 46,000 employee records. In a statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 12 November, the world’s largest contract chipmaker said it had “found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised”. It said the leaked information matched data stored in the system services of a third-party cloud provider, and was unrelated to its operations or to customer data. TSMC has not named the provider, however, and has not said how many people are affected.

The listing appeared on two underground forums, DarkForums and BreachForums, according to United Daily News and ETtoday . The seller is asking for 3 bitcoin, or about NT$7.4 million, for a 6.9GB data set, and has threatened to publish everything if no buyer comes forward within a week. A sample file of 499 records, each with 19 fields, was posted alongside the listing, United Daily News reported. Neither TSMC nor Taiwanese media have verified that the full set holds 46,000 records.

According to the seller’s listing, as described in Taiwanese reports, each record includes a name, date of birth, job title, nationality, national ID number, home address, mobile number and email address. Some records reportedly also contain bank account information, along with the phone numbers and addresses of employees’ emergency contacts. TSMC’s own statement does not list the fields involved, although it says the company is informing affected staff and providing them with support. A national ID number combined with a bank account and a home address is enough for convincing impersonation attempts against banks and mobile operators. That is why the exposure matters even without a breach of TSMC’s network.

The profile of the people involved also makes the data unusually valuable. TSMC’s engineers are among the most sought-after in the chip industry, and job titles tied to names and phone numbers are useful material for targeted phishing and recruitment approaches. Taiwanese prosecutors charged several people in 2025 over the alleged theft of trade secrets linked to TSMC’s 2nm process, a case that showed how much outsiders will invest to reach the company’s staff. TSMC said it is working with the cloud vendor, the relevant investigating authorities and a third-party cybersecurity firm to establish the facts.

For gamers and the wider hardware market, TSMC’s key claim is that the incident does not touch its fabs. The company makes most of the world’s most advanced chips, including Nvidia’s GeForce and data centre GPUs and AMD’s Ryzen and Radeon processors. It also builds Apple’s A and M series chips and the custom processors inside the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles. TSMC said the data is unrelated to its operations, and Taiwanese reports said there was no evidence that wafer production or customer orders were affected. So far, there is no sign of any knock-on effect on the supply of PC or console hardware, which is already under pressure from rising memory costs .

TSMC has dealt with security incidents before, although the earlier ones followed a different pattern. In August 2018, a virus spread through several of its fabs after what the company called “misoperation during the software installation process for a new tool”. TSMC estimated the impact at about 3% of its third-quarter revenue. In 2023, the LockBit ransomware group claimed to have hacked TSMC, but the company said the incident hit a hardware supplier and exposed only server set-up information. The latest case again points to a third party, this time a cloud provider holding employee records.

title: Microsoft Outage Passes 16 Hours With Outlook and Teams Still Down, but Xbox Is Holding Up
content:
Microsoft’s outage across Outlook, Teams and the wider Microsoft 365 suite has now run for more than 16 hours, and the company’s own status page still shows service capacity below normal. Problems began with Teams in North America on 12 November, before Exchange Online mailboxes started failing from 17:54 UTC (11:24 pm IST). Minutes later, Microsoft confirmed that the issue could affect Microsoft 365 connectivity “for users in any region”. For gamers, the main question is whether Xbox has gone down with it, and so far the answer is mostly no.

As of Friday morning UTC, the official Xbox status page listed all services as “up and running”, including sign-in, multiplayer, the store and cloud gaming. Microsoft’s service health page names Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote, Microsoft To Do, Teams and Microsoft 365 for the web among the affected consumer products, and Xbox is not on that list. The disruption sits mainly in Exchange Online, the email system behind Outlook, and in the services that depend on it.

Some players have still reported trouble since the outage began. Users on social media and outage trackers have described failed sign-ins, digital games that would not launch, cloud saves that did not sync and problems reaching Xbox Cloud Gaming. Windows Central, which collected those reports, said its own staff could connect normally. Microsoft has not confirmed those reports, and TalkEsport found no post from Xbox Support about the outage. Players who see errors should check the status page first, since a local network fault can produce the same errors.

The timing is awkward for Xbox, which has only just widened access to cloud play. Microsoft launched a free, ad-supported tier of Xbox Cloud Gaming on 12 November, the same day the outage began, and cloud gaming depends on Microsoft’s servers more than any other part of the platform. Xbox was not so lucky in October 2025, when a faulty configuration change to Azure Front Door took down Xbox sign-ins and Minecraft for hours along with Microsoft 365. Cloud failures have hit games elsewhere too, including Google Cloud’s outage in Europe last month.

Microsoft has given a detailed running account of the incident, though not a root cause. At 22:09 UTC on 12 November, it said a core process on affected servers was “becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss”, and that its actions so far “have not provided the anticipated relief”. Two hours later, it said servers it had returned to service could become unresponsive again “once they receive traffic”. It then began limiting which types of traffic could reach the affected infrastructure.

There has been some movement on the cause since then. Microsoft first said it had not identified any recent change linked to the start of the problem. By 21:40 UTC, however, it was assessing whether reverting “a small number of recent configuration updates” could speed up recovery. On Friday morning, it reported “positive results for service stability and increased capacity” from traffic optimisation, and said it was extending those actions across affected regions. Its latest update said service health “remains variable”, and that it has no evidence of malicious activity.

title: Culper Research Shorted Nvidia Over China in May, Stock Is Down 26% Since
content:
On 13 May, Culper Research published a 40-page report arguing that Nvidia had “a significant China problem”, and disclosed that it was short the stock. Investors largely ignored the warning for the next five months. Nvidia closed 2.3% higher that day at $225.83, gained another 4.4% to $235.74 the next session, and went on to close at a high of $239.24 on 6 October. By Thursday’s close of $166.19, the shares were 26% below their level on the day of the report and more than 30% below that October peak.

The six months in between have turned parts of Culper’s case from short-seller allegations into mainstream reporting. Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive whom the report described as “uncomfortably close” to Jensen Huang, is now at the centre of the scandal that ended his 33-year run as Nvidia’s chief executive. Megaspeed, which Culper called Nvidia’s largest buyer in Southeast Asia, is under investigation in Singapore and has hired a US law firm to count its GPUs . None of that proves Culper’s core financial argument, which concerns how much of Nvidia’s revenue still depends on Chinese demand.

The report’s central claim is that Nvidia’s China business never really went to zero. Huang said in October 2025 that Nvidia had gone from a 95% share of China’s market to nothing, and that the company was “100% out of China”. Culper estimated that more than 20% of Nvidia’s fiscal 2026 compute revenue was still driven by Chinese demand, through illegal diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries. Nvidia has not publicly addressed that estimate, and no regulator has published a figure of its own.

The mechanics matter because of how Nvidia reports its sales. Its filings assign revenue to the customer’s billing location, and Nvidia has said that “end customer and shipping location may be different” from that location. According to the Wall Street Journal’s Jonathan Weil, Nvidia stopped breaking out Singapore revenue after the quarter that ended in July 2025, when the country accounted for 22% of the total. Nvidia has said shipments into Singapore itself were insignificant, but its filings do not say where the rest of that hardware went.

Culper then followed the money through Megaspeed’s accounts. It said the company’s balance sheet grew from about $33 million at the end of 2023 to $3.0 billion a year later, mostly through $2.9 billion of “refundable deposits” from an unnamed source. The report alleged that documents pointed to Alibaba as the financier, through a Singapore company called Apex Enterprise Solutions. It also said Megaspeed’s Malaysian unit, Speedmatrix, imported $4.6 billion of products between December 2024 and January 2026. About $4 billion of that came from Aivres, an Nvidia server partner that took over the US business of China’s Inspur.

Nvidia and Megaspeed both reject the diversion claims made in the report. Nvidia said in October that the allegations against Megaspeed had been “thoroughly investigated and debunked last year”, and that Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected”. Megaspeed says reviews by the US Commerce Department, Malaysian authorities and Nvidia found no evidence of violations, and it has threatened legal action over a Bloomberg report that it rented computing power to Alibaba. No charges have been reported against Nvidia, Megaspeed or Alice Huang.

title: Viral ‘Nvidia Employees’ Letter Demanding Jensen Huang’s Return Is a Copy of OpenAI’s 2023 Letter
content:
A post claiming that “hundreds of NVIDIA employees” have signed an internal letter demanding Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive was shared widely on X on Friday. The letter shown in the post also demands the resignation of Nvidia’s board and threatens a mass move to “the SpaceX Terafab initiative under the leadership of Jensen Huang and Elon Musk”. The first names on its signature list belong to several of Nvidia’s best-known technical leaders. There is no evidence that this letter is real.

Its wording follows, almost line for line, the letter OpenAI employees sent to their own board in November 2023, after Sam Altman was removed as chief executive. The developer’s account that shared it has not said where the letter came from. About seven hours earlier, the same account had described this exact scenario as a way for Huang to win back his job “like Sam did with the OpenAI coup”. In that version, Musk offers Huang work at Terafab and jobs for Nvidia staff, employees threaten to follow him, and Huang returns to restructure the board.

A reader note now shown on the post says that no reports confirm a signed letter like the one in the image, but the letter has kept travelling. Several crypto and finance news sites republished it on Friday as an “alleged” petition, while noting that its authenticity had not been confirmed. TalkEsport has found no public comment on the letter from Nvidia itself.

Huang’s departure, unlike the letter, is a matter of record. Nvidia announced on 12 November that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after 33 years in charge. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive, and former Synopsys chief executive Harvey Jones was named the company’s first board chair, according to Nvidia’s official announcement . TalkEsport is not repeating the names on the viral letter, because nothing shows that any of those executives signed it.

Placed side by side, the two letters share their structure, their arguments and many of their sentences. Only the company names, the people and the rival employer have changed. The OpenAI letter, which was widely reported in November 2023, was eventually signed by 745 of the company’s 770 employees.

Several details in the viral letter also clash with the public record. It says the board “terminated” Huang, while Nvidia’s announcement and its filing with US regulators say he resigned. It claims that Elon Musk has promised jobs to every Nvidia employee, but TalkEsport found no such statement from Musk or SpaceX. Musk’s only public remark about hiring Huang so far was that it “would be an honour” . Terafab itself is real, a chip factory costing about $20 billion that Tesla and SpaceX announced in March for Austin, Texas, but nothing shows that Huang has joined it.

title: OpenAI Backs China Chip Curbs as Jensen Huang Exits Nvidia, but the ‘Targeted Takedown’ Claim Does Not Hold Up
content:
On the day Jensen Huang left Nvidia, Bloomberg reported that OpenAI had told US lawmakers it supports a bipartisan push to tighten China’s access to AI chips. The package also targets the tools used to make those chips, and the report was published on 12 November. The timing has fuelled a viral claim on X that Huang’s departure was “a targeted takedown” by OpenAI and Anthropic, which are said to have formed an alliance to back the curbs. The public record does not support that claim.

OpenAI’s support follows months of review, according to reports, and Anthropic has campaigned openly for chip export controls since at least 2025. Versions of the proposals now in Congress were also being debated well before Huang’s private life became a story. What has changed is that Nvidia’s most powerful opponent of those controls is no longer running the company.

Huang resigned on 12 November after a week of reports about his relationships, including with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China. Nvidia’s board had hired former federal prosecutor Joon Kim to investigate his conduct. Nothing in the reporting so far links his departure to OpenAI, Anthropic or the export debate, and the photo of Sam Altman and Dario Amodei shared with the viral claim could not be verified.

According to Bloomberg, OpenAI told lawmakers this week that it would support a package of export-related measures that Congress is weighing. Reports describe three parts to the package, each aimed at a different gap in the current rules. One would give Congress more power to review exports of advanced AI chips, and another would track where those chips end up to curb smuggling and diversion. A third would press US allies to restrict exports of chipmaking equipment to China. Lawmakers are considering attaching the measures to the annual defence bill, the National Defense Authorization Act, which must pass each year.

Nvidia has fought similar efforts before, and won. In December 2025, Congress dropped a proposal to curb chip exports from the defence bill, in what Bloomberg described as a lobbying win for Nvidia. Huang had argued for years that selling to China keeps the country dependent on American technology, and the White House has largely sided with him on chip sales. Nvidia and trade groups oppose the new package too, arguing that stricter limits would burden Nvidia and the wider industry, according to reports.

The political ground has shifted since then, largely because of the Megaspeed affair. The chairs of three House committees asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on his reported link to Alice Huang, and Singapore has said it barred her from re-entry after she gave police inaccurate information. Semafor reported on 12 November that Congress is now pushing for tighter export controls following the Nvidia scandal.

title: Jensen Huang Called Colette Kress a ‘Deer in the Headlights’ Months Before She Replaced Him, WSJ Reports
content:
Months before Colette Kress replaced him as Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang belittled her in front of the company’s top finance team, according to a Wall Street Journal report by Anissa Gardizy and Robbie Whelan. At a meeting in August, Huang called Kress “a deer in the headlights” while interrupting her presentation, according to a person familiar with the comments. He also described her as a “reporting CFO”, rather than someone who could help him define a strategy or make decisions, the Journal reports.

Kress became interim chief executive on 12 November, when Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned after 33 years in charge.

The report also sheds light on the business pressures Huang was dealing with before the scandal broke. According to the Journal, he had summoned his senior finance executives to diagnose what it calls a “ballooning problem”. Nvidia was in talks to provide billions of dollars of guarantees to companies that could not afford its chips, and Huang was starting to question whether the dealmaking spree he had launched had gone too far. The Journal’s subheadline says Kress, now in charge, has questioned some of that dealmaking.

Some of the guarantee deals were led by Huang’s son-in-law, who works at Nvidia, according to the Journal. He had been offering financing to upstart cloud providers and data centre developers, in the hope of turning them into long-term Nvidia customers. TalkEsport is not naming him, as he is not a public figure, although the Journal identifies him.

During the same August meeting, Huang described a difficult picture for the company, the Journal reports. Major cloud providers were running away from Nvidia, he said, making plans to use alternative chips and reduce their reliance on the firm. The largest of those providers already build their own AI processors, such as Google’s Tensor Processing Units and Amazon’s Trainium chips. Huang also said that the supply of chip wafers and memory Nvidia had committed to buy was coming at him “like an avalanche”.

Those comments matter because they come from inside the company, and from Huang himself. They suggest that he saw financing and supply commitments as a growing risk months before his personal life became the story. The Journal’s account relies on people familiar with the matter, and TalkEsport has not found a public response from Kress, Huang or Nvidia to the report.

title: Singapore Barred Alice Huang From Re-Entry After She Gave Police Inaccurate Information, MHA Says
content:
Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country in February, after police concluded that she had given them information she knew to be inaccurate, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on 12 November. In a statement on its investigations into the cloud company Megaspeed, the ministry described her as Megaspeed’s then chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers.

Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed offences linked to Megaspeed’s possible false declarations, but gave her a stern warning. The ministry added that she “was not based in Singapore, and was not investigated for espionage”.

Alice Huang has been named in reports as the woman with whom Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had a relationship, and US intelligence reportedly suspects her of gathering information for China. No charges have been reported against her, and Beijing has rejected the espionage claims as smears. Singapore’s statement does not mention Nvidia or Jensen Huang, whose board is reportedly preparing to remove him . It is Singapore’s most detailed public account of the case so far.

The ministry’s timeline starts in February 2025, when the Singapore Police Force and Singapore Customs opened an investigation into several companies and key officers, including Megaspeed. The case concerns potential false declarations in the purchase of servers, along with related offences. Home Affairs Minister K Shanmugam said in March 2025 that the investigation was not based on any request from another country. Megaspeed itself began operating in its current form in March 2023, when Alice Huang was listed as its managing director.

US officials visited Megaspeed a few months later, in the middle of 2025. On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a voluntary post-shipment verification check at the company, with Alice Huang present. The ministry said that was Singapore’s first sign of US interest in Megaspeed and in her. Singapore police interviewed her on the same day, and impounded her passport to make sure she attended further questioning. Police returned the passport on 26 February 2026, and she left Singapore that day.

By then, police had concluded that she had provided information she knew to be inaccurate, in order to downplay her role in Megaspeed. She was given a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country, and the ministry said other cases had been dealt with in a similar way in the past. The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is still continuing. None of those six people has been in Singapore since it began in February 2025, according to the ministry.

title: Jensen Huang Had Third Relationship, With Second Nvidia Employee, Sources Say
content:
Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, two sources told Reuters on 12 November. The allegation is the third relationship linked to Huang in less than two weeks. The woman has not been named, and her role at the company has not been disclosed. Reuters could not reach her for comment.

The allegation emerged on the same day Nvidia said Huang had stepped down after 33 years as chief executive. Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive while keeping her finance role. Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who has sat on Nvidia’s board since 1993, was named the company’s first chair.

Huang admitted on 8 November that he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, Lori Huang, in a letter to Nvidia staff that the company also issued as a press release. He apologised and said the board had opened an independent investigation, which he supported. The letter did not name anyone or say how many relationships were involved.

The admission followed weeks of scrutiny over Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US and Singapore authorities investigated Megaspeed in 2025 over suspected breaches of chip export controls. Claims that US officials suspect Alice Huang of working for China’s Ministry of State Security have not been confirmed, and she has not commented publicly. Nvidia said on 29 October that Huang’s meetings with her were “not unusual or unexpected” for a chief executive.

On 11 November, five former and current Nvidia staff alleged that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. That allegation remains unconfirmed. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not commented on it.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% at the open on 12 November, their lowest level since June 2025. The stock recovered part of the loss and closed at $166.19, down 4.34%. The fall cut Nvidia’s market value from $4.498 trillion to $4.005 trillion. Shares had already dropped more than 5% on 9 November, the first trading day after Huang’s letter.

title: BETBY becomes first company to receive ESIC’s CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation
content:
The Esports Integrity Commission (ESIC) has awarded BETBY the first CPU v CPU Gold Standard accreditation , recognizing the betting provider’s effort and commitment to comply with ESIC’s integrity requirements for automated esports competitions.

The certification follows an on-site audit, an assessment of additional evidence, and an independent audit review conducted in August 2026. BETBY will also undergo annual audit reviews to maintain its accreditation.

The recognition marks the first time an organization has met the requirements under ESIC’s newly introduced framework, which aims to strengthen trust in automated esports competitions used in betting markets.

The CPU v CPU Gold Standard was introduced to address integrity concerns surrounding automated esports competitions, where match outcomes are generated by software rather than human players. Examples include virtual football and basketball matches, which have gained popularity in betting markets because they are available around the clock and typically take only a few minutes to finish.

According to ESIC, the framework establishes 17 mandatory control areas covering the systems responsible for generating and validating match results, the infrastructure supporting these competitions, and the personnel authorized to operate or modify them.

These requirements provide a basis for independently assessing how automated competitions are managed and whether the necessary safeguards are in place to protect their integrity.

title: Chovy, enfin en finale des Worlds : « Je veux profiter de ce moment »
content:
C’est un moment que Jeong « Chovy » Ji-hoon attend depuis le début de sa carrière. Après huit participations aux championnats du monde, le joueur de Gen.G a enfin décroché son billet pour la grande finale des Worlds 2026. Une qualification obtenue face à Invictus Gaming, au terme d’une rencontre durant laquelle les Sud-Coréens ont dû s’adapter au style particulièrement collectif de leurs adversaires. Dans un entretien accordé à Inven Global , Chovy est notamment revenu sur les ajustements réalisés en pleine partie pour répondre aux regroupements incessants de la formation chinoise.

Désormais, tous les regards sont tournés vers la finale, où Gen.G retrouvera le vainqueur du duel entre T1 et Bilibili Gaming. Deux adversaires que Chovy refuse de départager. « Dès que T1 est dans l’équation, il est impossible de faire des pronostics » , explique-t-il. En attendant de connaître son opposant, le midlaner compte surtout peaufiner sa préparation, malgré l’absence d’équipes disponibles pour disputer des scrims. Le travail se concentrera notamment sur la SoloQ et l’analyse des drafts, un domaine dans lequel il estime que Gen.G possède actuellement un avantage sur ses concurrents.

Au-delà de l’enjeu sportif, cette première finale mondiale représente un accomplissement particulièrement émouvant pour Chovy. Après tant d’années à poursuivre ce rêve, le Sud-Coréen veut éviter de se laisser submerger par la pression. « J’ai atteint la finale après huit ans, et je pense que c’est un moment qui ne se reproduira peut-être jamais. Je ne veux pas laisser la nervosité ou l’anxiété me gâcher un moment aussi important » , confie-t-il, avant d’ajouter : « Je veux profiter de ce moment qui n’arrivera peut-être qu’une seule fois et remporter le championnat. »

Le joueur a également profité de cet entretien pour adresser un message touchant à sa mère, qui l’accompagne depuis ses débuts. « Même si je ne l’exprime pas beaucoup extérieurement, ma mère m’aide énormément. Parfois, elle me sert de modèle dans ma vie » , raconte-t-il, avant de la remercier avec une certaine pudeur. À une victoire du titre mondial, Chovy n’a désormais plus qu’une marche à gravir pour transformer huit années d’efforts en consécration historique.

title: Genshin Impact Cheater Selling Paid Stygian Onslaught Carries Reportedly Arrested While Meeting Customers

The arrest has not been confirmed by police or by HoYoverse, the game’s developer. The player’s name, the city and the date of the arrest have not been disclosed.

Security camera images from inside the store , dated 3 November, circulated online alongside the claims. A second image showed a Chinese-language apology to HoYoverse on a phone screen. Neither the police nor HoYoverse has commented publicly on the case.

In the apology, the player admitted to posting videos of themselves “using cheats in Genshin Impact” without authorisation. The player said the actions “seriously violated” the official rules of miHoYo and Genshin Impact, which prohibit cheating. The player has since deleted the posts that advertised the service.

The player promoted the service through videos on Bilibili that showed the cheats in use. The videos directed viewers to a store on Xianyu, a Chinese second-hand marketplace, that sold the boosting service. Prices for the service have not been disclosed.

Stygian Onslaught is a combat challenge in Genshin Impact made up of three timed battles. Higher difficulty levels add tougher enemies and stricter time limits, and the mode rewards players who clear them quickly. The allegations first surfaced on the Chinese gaming forum NGA before spreading on other platforms.

HoYoverse said in March 2026 that it removed more than one million illegal links and pieces of content during 2025, including cheat software and pirated resources. In 2023, the company threatened legal action against cheaters after malicious plug-ins affected other players’ accounts.

title: Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic is playable and in final polish, Druckmann says
content:
Naughty Dog's Neil Druckmann says that Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet has reached the final stage of production, with the game now playable, Inven Global reported. It's the first proper status check we’ve had on the PS5 project since its reveal, and it seems that all systems are go.

Druckmann, the studio head and the game's director and writer were speaking at Comic Creators Block Party 2026. Host and comedian Patton Oswalt asked for more details but Druckmann was keen to keep his lips sealed where the story is concerned.

"We've only teased it, so I can't talk too much about it," he said before adding "we're kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we're refining it and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world."

While he may be resistant to saying much more at the moment, Druckmann reassured Oswalt and everyone else that the studio will reveal more next year. "We're going to show gameplay, more of the story," he revealed, which fits an earlier September update when Naughty Dog said it needed "to cook for just a little bit longer."

No release date or window has been given, though, and for now only PS5 is a confirmed platform, where Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet will be published by Sony Interactive Entertainment.

Despite expressing reluctance to dive deeper into the story, Druckmann fed fans a few crumbs when he described the new game as a mix of Jak and Daxter, The Last of Us and action-adventure title Uncharted. He says the team were eager to recreate the sci-fi and fantasy of Jak and Daxter, while mixing in the pulp adventure of Uncharted, before ramping things up with the punishing drama of The Last of Us . If all this is accurate, it’ll be the studio’s first sci-fi-tinged outing since Jak and Daxter.

The response followed an Instagram story Jonathan posted after Kronten’s stream, which read “I choose me, I’m sorry”. The line is from Kendrick Lamar’s song “Mirror”. Jonathan did not explain the story or say whether it was a reply to Kronten.

Kronten made the allegations during a livestream in early November. title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After 33 Years; Colette Kress Named Interim Chief
content:
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and turned a graphics-card maker for PC gamers into the company at the centre of the AI boom, is no longer its chief executive. On Thursday, 12 November, Nvidia announced that Huang has resigned as president, CEO and a member of the board , effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress takes over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The announcement ends a week in which the pressure on Huang kept building. It started with questions over his relationship with an executive whom US officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Then came his own written admission to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, followed by fresh allegations about a second relationship, this time inside Nvidia. The board met on Wednesday night to decide his future, and the meeting ran into the evening. By Thursday morning in California, the most famous leather jacket in tech had left the building. Nvidia’s statement gives no reason for the departure, although the timing leaves little room for interpretation.

The unravelling began in late October, when The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data-centre company Megaspeed. Megaspeed is an Nvidia customer, and it was already under investigation by US and Singaporean authorities over suspected chip-export violations. According to the Times, a US intelligence memo had alleged that she was working for China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has dismissed those claims as baseless, and Nvidia’s first response was that Huang’s interactions with her were “not unusual or unexpected” for a CEO who meets customers.

That line did not hold for long. On Sunday, 8 November, Huang wrote to employees admitting that he had been unfaithful to his wife of 40 years and apologising. The note named no one. On the same day, Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into whether he had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. It also said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised. Two days later, the independent directors brought in former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim and his firm to run the review. Then, on Wednesday, the Times reported a second affair, citing current and former employees, this time with a senior Nvidia executive who reports directly to Huang. Neither Nvidia nor Huang has confirmed that report. Within hours, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove him.

Washington was also closing in. Three House Republican committee chairmen, John Moolenaar, Brian Mast and Rick Crawford, had asked Huang for a closed-door briefing on his ties to Alice Huang. They also warned that a subpoena could follow if he did not respond. Meanwhile, Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons asked the administration to preserve Nvidia’s China-related records. President Donald Trump stood by Huang throughout, calling him “an honorable guy” and saying he should stay on. In the end, however, the decision belonged to Nvidia’s board, and Huang had little power to resist it. He owns roughly 3.6% of the company, so unlike founders at Meta or SpaceX, he had no majority voting control to fall back on.

Colette Kress has been Nvidia’s executive vice president and CFO since September 2013. Before that, she spent nearly 25 years in finance at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. She keeps the CFO job alongside the top role. In Nvidia’s statement, she said she is committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” The board also named Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, as the company’s first-ever chair. That is a telling change for a company that, until this week, had no board chair at all. According to Jones, the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team” and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to carry on without interruption. The search for a permanent CEO will look at both internal and external candidates.

title: Call of Duty Ranked Levels: Every Skill Division and What Carries Into a New Title
content:
Call of Duty ranked levels in mainline multiplayer Ranked Play run from Bronze to a Top 250 leaderboard finish. Black Ops 7 treats a new season differently depending on whether you finished below Platinum, and a new title begins its own progression. Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile have separate ranked systems.

Black Ops 7 Ranked Play has seven named Skill Divisions that group players by rank, followed by Top 250, a place on the leaderboard for the highest-ranked competitors. In order, the eight ladder positions are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Crimson, Iridescent, and Top 250. Top 250 is a leaderboard position rather than another ordinary division to grind through. As a new player, you’ll receive a starting rank only after winning the required placement matches.

This is the Black Ops 7 multiplayer ladder; Warzone and Call of Duty Mobile use their own ranked systems.

Players in the Bronze division through Gold keep their rank and SR when a new season starts, but players in Platinum and above need a placement win. Rank is only part of what a profile carries, though: building one from scratch with the level, weapons, and camos you want takes a long run of matches. Players who would rather start from a finished profile can browse Call of Duty accounts on Skycoach , a marketplace where each Black Ops 7, Modern Warfare 4, or Warzone account listing shows whether it is ranked-ready, along with its level, Prestige, camo count, weapons, and the platforms it links to (PC, PlayStation, or Xbox). Skycoach has operated since 2020, and purchases come with buyer protection: a warranty period, a refund policy, and 24/7 support.

Black Ops 7 starts with placements. You must win three placement matches to receive a starting rank, and after each placement win, the Minimum Starting Rank updates to show a projection of where you’re expected to land.

After a Ranked Play win, you gain Skill Rating (SR), which sets your position on the ladder. The amount isn’t fixed: it depends on your match performance relative to the skill of the other players and the team’s margin of victory. The same factors affect SR deducted after a loss. As Activision’s ranked support page explains, the SR change depends on these match factors, so two wins during the same evening can award different amounts without an error in the display.

title: Alice Huang’s husband, a video game investor, introduced her to Jensen Huang, report suggests
content:
Jensen Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by her own husband, according to a new report by the Wall Street Journal’s Lingling Wei. The husband, a Chinese businessman, had known the Nvidia chief executive for about a decade before making the introduction. When the two men first met in the 2010s, he was a private equity investor focused on video game companies, at a time when Nvidia was still best known for PC gaming graphics cards.

The Journal reports that he is also Alice Huang’s business partner, and that he appeared to accept her romantic relationship with Huang. According to people familiar with the couple, he spoke openly about her closeness to the Nvidia chief.

The report adds a new layer to a scandal that has already put Huang’s job at risk. Huang admitted to an affair in a letter to staff on 8 November, without naming the person involved. Reports have since linked him to Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China. Nvidia’s board is reportedly preparing to remove him , although it has not announced a decision, and no charges have been reported against Alice Huang.

The Journal’s account places the start of the story in the games business. According to the report, the husband got to know Huang while investing in video game companies, years before Nvidia’s data centre chips made it the most valuable chip company in the world. Over the past decade, the couple then moved between business ventures in video game companies, pharmaceutical takeovers and cloud computing, the Journal says. The report does not give an exact date for when Huang and Alice Huang first met.

Video games also run through the wider Megaspeed story. Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked, was set up in Singapore in 2023 as an offshore unit of 7Road, according to a New York Times investigation. The parent company is a Chinese games and cloud firm, best known for browser games such as DDTank and Wartune. That background, along with its purchases of billions of dollars of Nvidia hardware, is part of why Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal . The Journal’s report does not link the husband to Megaspeed or 7Road.

TalkEsport is not naming the husband, who is a private individual, although the Journal identifies him. The report relies on people familiar with the couple, and TalkEsport has not found any public comment from him or from Alice Huang. Nvidia previously described Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang as “not unusual”, saying he meets thousands of customer executives every year. Beijing has rejected the espionage claims as smears against China.

title: GTA 6 Release Time for All Regions: When GTA 6 Unlocks Worldwide
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI unlocks at midnight local time on 19 November in every region, on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games is using a rolling regional release rather than a single global launch. New Zealand is first, at 11:00 UTC on 18 November. The US West Coast is last, at 08:00 UTC on 19 November, a gap of 21 hours.

The table shows when GTA VI unlocks in major cities, in local time and in UTC. Players in the same time zone as a listed city get the game at the same moment. In India, the game unlocks at 12:00 AM IST on 19 November, matching the PlayStation and Xbox India store listings.

The UTC times are our calculations based on midnight in each city, using standard time for 19 November. Countries that span several time zones, such as Australia, Brazil, Mexico and the US, unlock at local midnight in each zone. Rockstar has not published an official city-by-city unlock table.

The game unlocks automatically for players who pre-ordered digitally and finished the pre-load. Pre-loading opened on 10 November, and the game needs up to 212 GB of free space, as Rockstar’s pre-load FAQ states. Players who have not pre-loaded must download the full game after it unlocks. That can take hours on slower connections, as we covered in our report on GTA 6 pre-load times and file size .

Retail boxes contain a download code rather than a disc. Owners of physical editions still need to download the game, and Rockstar has not said whether any stores will open at midnight. GTA VI is available only on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch. Xbox One owners can play through Xbox Cloud Gaming, as we covered in our report on GTA 6 coming to Xbox One through the cloud .

Some players plan to switch their console region to New Zealand to start 21 hours earlier. Rockstar has not commented on the practice. The method differs between PS5 and Xbox, as we covered in our report on playing GTA 6 early with the New Zealand trick . Rockstar has not announced a PC version or a PC release date.

title: Sky Esports Win G2 x PUBG MOBILE Community Challenge on a Dust II-Inspired Map, Undisputed
content:
Amateur squad Sky Esports has won the G2 x PUBG MOBILE Community Challenge, a tournament played on a custom map inspired by Counter-Strike’s Dust II inside PUBG MOBILE. The team beat Star Dust Esports 2-0 in the best-of-three grand final over the weekend of 7 and 8 November, and took home €500 in cash, a €125 Amazon gift card and G2 merchandise.

Twenty-five teams entered the event, which was open only to amateur players and ran in a round-based bomb-defusal mode rather than PUBG MOBILE’s usual battle royale. The winners are not to be confused with Skyesports, the Indian tournament organiser.

The tournament opened on Saturday with best-of-one, single-elimination qualifiers, which left no room for an off day. With 25 teams chasing four semi-final places, a single defeat ended a team’s weekend. Sky Esports, WM Officials, Star Dust Esports and DMSXBIS came through to claim those slots. On Sunday, both semi-finals were played as best-of-three series, and both ended 2-0, with Sky Esports beating WM Officials and Star Dust Esports knocking out DMSXBIS.

The grand final was just as one-sided as the semi-finals. Sky Esports took the opening map and then won the second 6-1 to complete a 2-0 series win, according to the organisers. In the third-place match, played alongside the final, DMSXBIS beat WM Officials to finish on the podium. That means Sky Esports won every match it played across the two days, from the single-elimination qualifiers to the final.

Every team in the top four left with a prize. The cash prizes add up to the €1,000 prize pool that G2’s community account advertised when registration opened on 27 October. On top of that, the top three teams each received a €125 Amazon gift card and G2 merchandise, while fourth place took €125 in gift cards.

The custom map was the event’s main hook for Counter-Strike fans. Called PMG2, it was built in World of Wonder, the creation mode in PUBG MOBILE that lets players and partners design their own maps and game modes. Its layout is inspired by Dust II, one of the best-known maps in Counter-Strike’s history. To keep the Counter-Strike feel, teams played a classic bomb-defusal mode in which each player had a single life per match, according to the organisers.

title: Megaspeed Hires a US Law Firm to Count Its GPUs
content:
Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company at the centre of the Nvidia espionage reports, has hired a US law firm to count its graphics processors and independently check whether it complied with US export controls. In an official statement dated 12 November on its website , chairman and chief executive Tan Yong Pong said the company had cooperated with inspections by the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). He added that Megaspeed “stands ready to cooperate fully” with any other relevant US authority, and that it “welcomes appropriate government scrutiny”. It is the company’s first public statement since reports linked Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of gathering information for China.

The statement runs to four short paragraphs, signed by Tan as chairman and chief executive of Megaspeed International, and it leaves a great deal out. It does not mention Nvidia, Jensen Huang or Alice Huang, and it does not name the law firm, which it describes only as “a leading U.S. law firm”. It also gives no start date for the GPU census, and does not say whether the findings will be published. Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, has still not announced a decision on Huang, whom it is reportedly preparing to remove after a second affair report.

The tone is very different from Megaspeed’s previous public response. In December 2025, after a Bloomberg investigation into chip smuggling concerns, the company said it operated “fully within the bounds” of export control rules. It said inspections by BIS, Malaysia’s trade ministry and Nvidia itself had found no violations, and it did not rule out legal action against Bloomberg. The new statement repeats that Megaspeed cooperated with BIS inspections, but it makes no claim about what those inspections found.

BIS is the US agency that enforces export controls on advanced chips. Instead of repeating its earlier assurances, the company has handed an outside law firm the job of counting its GPUs and verifying its “export control compliance practices”. In export cases, the central question is usually where controlled chips ended up, and a full inventory is one way to answer it. US officials reportedly found Nvidia servers and GPUs still sealed in their crates when they inspected a Malaysian site linked to Megaspeed in late 2024. US lawmakers have since put the company’s Nvidia hardware imports at more than $4.6 billion.

Megaspeed itself grew out of the games industry. According to a New York Times investigation from October 2025, it was set up in Singapore in 2023 as an offshore unit of 7Road, a Chinese games and cloud company. The parent is backed by state investors and is best known for browser games such as DDTank and Wartune. That background, along with its rapid rise as an Nvidia customer, explains why Megaspeed sits at the centre of the Huang scandal . Its website now presents it as a specialised GPU cloud provider, advertising Nvidia GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 systems from offices in Singapore and Jakarta.

US scrutiny of Megaspeed began more than a year before the Huang scandal. Senator Tom Cotton asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to investigate the company in an October 2025 letter , writing that it had received billions of dollars of US chips, “potentially violating U.S. export laws”. Megaspeed reportedly stopped ordering Nvidia hardware in July 2025, as investigations widened, and Alice Huang was reported to have left around the same time. Singapore police have said that their own inquiry concerns Megaspeed’s compliance with local law, not Alice Huang personally.

title: Elon Musk Says Hiring Jensen Huang “Would Be an Honour” Amid Nvidia Board Reports

Musk’s reply came on the same day that reports said Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet and discuss Huang’s future at the company. Some of those reports said directors were considering removing him. Nvidia has not announced any change to its leadership. The board has not commented publicly on the reports, and Huang remains chief executive.

Musk runs Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Several of his companies, including Tesla and xAI, use Nvidia’s AI computing hardware. His reply is not a job offer. Musk has not said which company Huang might join, or in what role. Huang has not responded to the post.

Musk has commented on Huang before. Earlier this month his “you’re an asset” joke about Huang spread online, and we traced how Musk’s joke became a meme . We have also looked at who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia.

Huang, 63, told staff in an email on 8 November that he had had an extramarital affair. Nvidia’s board opened an investigation the same day, led by a committee of independent directors. title: Krafton Releases Its Own On-Device AI Model, Raon-1 Nano, After Building PUBG Ally on Nvidia’s
content:
Krafton, the company behind PUBG: Battlegrounds and Battlegrounds Mobile India, has released Raon-1 nano, a small language model built for on-device inference. It has an effective 1.5 billion parameters and 3.1 billion in total, and the weights are on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence, which allows commercial use. Krafton says it was trained for multi-turn conversation, instruction following and tool calling, in Korean and English. For gamers, the relevant detail is that Krafton’s two shipped AI characters, PUBG Ally and inZOI’s Smart Zois, run on small models from Nvidia rather than on a model of Krafton’s own.

We’re releasing Raon-1 nano, an effective 1.5B dense LLM with per-layer embeddings and 3.1B total parameters. Our journey from PUBG Ally toward on-device LLMs continues. We pruned and distilled Raon-1 mini preview (30B-A4B) using our MoE-to-Dense approach, then further… pic.twitter.com/ydiQGrBlAd

KRAFTON AI, the company’s research arm, described the release as the next step in “our journey from PUBG Ally toward on-device LLMs”. Kangwook Lee, Krafton’s chief AI officer, said the company “finally” has “a better base model for our edge AI applications”, meaning models that run on local hardware such as a gaming PC. Krafton has not said which of its games will use Raon-1 nano, or when.

Krafton has shipped on-device AI in its games since inZOI entered early access in March 2025. Its optional Smart Zoi feature drives the city’s residents with a 0.5-billion-parameter Mistral NeMo Minitron model from Nvidia’s ACE platform, according to Nvidia , and it runs only on GeForce RTX graphics cards. PUBG Ally also uses Nvidia ACE, and its AI teammate Ella reached players in the Ally Duo beta on Sanhok in June 2026.

Krafton described Ally’s design in an engineering interview published by Nvidia . Its team first tested cloud-hosted models, but the combined network and inference latency made responses too slow for live squad play. It moved to Nvidia’s Mistral-NeMo-Minitron-2B, quantised it for client-side deployment and fitted it into the VRAM left over by PUBG, so Ally runs on GPUs with as little as 8GB. A separate Krafton research preprint put the median API cost of Claude Opus 4.8 at $7.10 per replayed match , and Krafton judged it impractical at scale.

The local approach still had limits in the beta. Ally Duo was restricted to PCs with GeForce RTX cards, and Krafton’s patch notes advised players who saw delayed responses to lower their graphics settings or resolution. That advice indicates the model and the game were competing for the same GPU resources.

title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang? Colette Kress, Ian Buck and Apple’s Johny Srouji Emerge
content:
Nvidia’s board is deciding who could run the company without Jensen Huang, and a short list of names has started to form. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is the leading option for an interim role, after Semafor reported that some directors favour appointing her if Huang is removed. Ian Buck, the Nvidia vice president who invented CUDA, is the internal engineer most often named for the longer term.

Outside the company, Apple’s chief hardware officer Johny Srouji and Arm chief executive Rene Haas have both been mentioned as possible candidates for the permanent job.

SCOOP: As Nvidia's board prepares to fire Jensen Huang, some members favor appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. https://t.co/3ZYayfzLMw

The board has not announced a decision on Huang’s future. Nvidia’s directors met late on Wednesday 11 November, according to Reuters, and Bloomberg reported that the board is working with an outside search firm to identify potential replacements. Nvidia has not commented on the succession talk, and Huang remains chief executive while the investigation led by former federal prosecutor Joon Kim continues. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led it ever since, so any successor would be the first new chief executive in the company’s 33 years.

Kress has been Nvidia’s chief financial officer since 2013, after senior finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Investors know her well from more than a decade of earnings calls, in which she has explained Nvidia’s rise from a graphics card maker to the world’s most valuable chip company. That familiarity counts for a lot in a crisis, especially with quarterly results due next week. She would also be the first woman to lead the company.

Her limits as a permanent leader are just as clear. Kress does not have an engineering background, which is why reports describe her as a caretaker rather than a long-term successor. Nvidia’s identity rests on its chips and software, and its next permanent leader will be expected to set the technical direction as Huang has done for three decades. An interim chief executive would buy the board time to run a proper search, which appears to be exactly what it has started doing.
